meaning: overcoat; a long, warm winter coat

senses.en: overcoat; a long, heavy coat worn over other clothes in cold weather

examples.en: It's cold out. Wear your coat.
examples.analysis: 大衣 is the object of 穿 'to wear': 穿 + 大衣. The first clause gives the reason, and 吧 at the end turns 穿大衣 into friendly advice rather than an order.

examples.en: How much is this coat?
examples.analysis: 这 + 件 + 大衣: between 这 'this' and a noun Chinese normally puts a measure word, and coats, shirts and other tops take 件. 多少钱 at the end asks the price, the standard line in a shop.

examples.en: I didn't bring my coat, and I'm a bit cold.
examples.analysis: 没 + 带 says the bringing did not happen: 没带大衣 'didn't bring my coat', with 大衣 as the object. 有点儿 + adjective adds a mild complaint: 有点儿冷 'a bit cold'.

related.en: coat; jacket (any outer layer, often shorter than a 大衣)

meaning: the north; the northern part of a country (in China: northern China)

senses.en: the north; the northern regions of a country
northern China, the northern part of the country (北方人 'a northerner')

examples.en: You're from the north, aren't you?
examples.analysis: 北方 describes 人 directly, with no 的: 北方人 'a northerner'. 吧 at the end of a statement asks for confirmation: the speaker is fairly sure and expects a yes.

examples.en: Winters in the north are very cold.
examples.analysis: 北方 + 的 + 冬天 = 'winter in the north': 的 links the place to the noun it describes. 冷 'cold' is the predicate with no 是, and 很 normally comes with an adjective in a plain statement like this.

examples.en: I've never been to the north.
examples.analysis: 北方 is the place after 去, with no word for 'to': 去 + place. 没 + verb + 过 says something has never happened up to now: 没去过 'have never been'.

related.en: the north side of a place; to the north of (北京北边)

meaning: young people; a young person (a young adult)

senses.en: young people as a group (现在的青年 'young people today')
a young person, usually a young adult (一个好青年)

examples.zh: 他是一个很有想法的青年。
examples.en: He's a young man with a lot of ideas of his own.
examples.analysis: 青年 is the noun at the end, and 很有想法 before 的 describes it: 'full of ideas of his own'. 一个 counts him as one young man. 青年 sounds a little more formal than 年轻人, the everyday word for young people.

examples.zh: 你们那儿的青年都去外地打工吗？
examples.en: Do all the young people where you're from go elsewhere to work?
examples.analysis: 那儿的 + 青年 'the young people there': 青年 means young people as a group. 都 sums up the whole group before the verbs, and 去外地打工 chains two actions: go elsewhere, then work.

examples.zh: 现在的青年人不太看电视了。
examples.en: Young people today don't watch much TV anymore.
examples.analysis: 现在的 + 青年人 = 'young people today'. In speech, 青年 meaning young people as a group often takes 人: 青年人. 不太 + verb softens the negative to 'not much', and 了 at the end marks a change from how things used to be.

related.en: young; 年轻人 is the everyday spoken word for young people
a boy or girl of roughly 10 to 16, younger than 青年

meaning: zoo

senses.en: zoo

examples.en: Let's go to the zoo this weekend.
examples.analysis: 动物园 is the destination right after 去, with no word for 'to'. The time word 周末 comes first, and 吧 makes the whole line a suggestion.

examples.en: Is the zoo far from here?
examples.analysis: This is the pattern for distance: A 离 B 远/近. 动物园 is the subject, 离这儿 'from here' sets the reference point, and 远 'far' is the predicate with no 是.

examples.en: I haven't been to the zoo in ages.
examples.analysis: 好久没 + verb + 了 = 'haven't done it for a long time'. 动物园 is the place after 去, and 了 at the end covers the whole stretch of time up to now.

hook: 动物 'animal' + 园 'garden, park'; 公园 'park' and 花园 'garden' end in the same 园.

meaning: from now on; in the future (counting from today)

senses.en: from now on; from this point forward (a time word)
the days ahead; the future (今后的工作 'the work ahead')

examples.en: From now on I'll come a little earlier.
examples.analysis: 今后 opens the sentence as a time word, 'from now on', which suits a promise after being late. 会 marks what the speaker will do, and 早一点儿 before 来 means 'a bit earlier'.

examples.en: What are your plans going forward?
examples.analysis: 今后 sits between the subject and the verb, the usual slot for time words. 打算 is a noun here, 'plan', the object of 有; 什么 makes it a question with no 吗.

examples.en: From now on, don't do that anymore, OK?
examples.analysis: 今后 + 别 makes the request cover every future occasion. 别…了 asks someone to stop doing something, 这样 'like this' points at what they did, and 好吗 softens it into a request.

related.en: after; later; can follow any event (下课以后), while 今后 counts only from now
before; in the past (the opposite direction in time from 今后)

meaning: at night; during the night

senses.en: at night; during the night (the dark hours, often while people sleep)

examples.en: Don't call me at night.
examples.analysis: 夜里 at the front sets when the request applies. 别 + verb makes a negative request, 'don't', and 给我打电话 'call me' uses 给 to mark who gets the call.

examples.en: Do you sleep well at night?
examples.analysis: 夜里 sits between the subject and the verb, the usual slot for time words. 睡得好 uses 得 to rate how the sleeping goes, and 吗 makes it a yes/no question, the kind a doctor asks.

examples.en: He didn't get home until 2 a.m.
examples.analysis: 夜里 + clock time places the hour in the night: 夜里两点 is 2 a.m. 才 before 回家 says it happened later than expected, like English 'not until'.

related.en: evening; night from dusk on (the everyday word); 夜里 is the later, darker hours
the middle of the night; around midnight

meaning: to work a part-time or temporary job; to work for wages

senses.en: to work a part-time or temporary job (students, holidays)
to work for someone else as a wage earner (去外地打工 'go elsewhere to find work')

examples.zh: 放假的时候我想去打工。
examples.en: I want to get a part-time job over the holidays.
examples.analysis: 去 + 打工 = 'go and work a temporary job', and 想 before them says what the speaker wants. 放假的时候 'during the holidays' sets the time at the front.

examples.en: Where's your part-time job?
examples.analysis: 在 + 哪儿 comes before the verb: Chinese puts where an action happens in front of it. 打工 takes no object; asked of a student, it means a part-time job.

examples.en: He works part-time while going to school.
examples.analysis: 一边 A 一边 B = doing A and B in the same period or at the same time. Here 上学 'go to school' and 打工 'work a casual job' run side by side.

collocations.en: to go and work (a casual job)
have done casual work (过 goes inside)
to leave home to find work

related.en: to work; a job (the general, neutral word)
to go to work; to be at work (a regular job)

meaning: by the time; when, once (some point arrives); until

senses.en: by the time; when (等到 + time or event, then the main clause)
wait until … (then …): 等到 … 再 + verb, wait for that point, then act

examples.en: By the time you got here, the food had gone cold.
examples.analysis: 等到 opens a time clause, 'by the time you came'. The main clause follows, and 都…了 means 'already': the food had gone cold. It is a mild complaint about being late.

examples.en: Let's wait till the holidays and go then.
examples.analysis: 等到 + an event, then 再 + verb: wait for that point and act after it. 再 here means 'then, only after that', not 'again'. 吧 makes it a suggestion.

examples.en: Once he's back, we'll leave.
examples.analysis: 等到 + 他回来 marks the moment the next step waits for. 就 in the main clause says the leaving follows right away: 'once he's back, we go'.

related.en: to wait; in speech 等 alone often does the same job (等你来了…)
time; …的时候 'when …' (any time, not a point waited for)

meaning: the majority; most (of a group)

senses.en: the majority; most (多数人 'most people')

examples.en: Most people think it's pretty good.
examples.analysis: 多数 goes straight before the noun, with no measure word or 的: 多数人 'most people'. 都 before the verb sums up that group, the majority, not everyone.

examples.en: Most of our class are girls.
examples.analysis: Here 多数 stands alone as the subject, 'the majority'. 我们班 'our class' is the topic, then 多数 + 是 + 女生 says what most of them are.

examples.zh: 你们公司多数人几点下班？
examples.en: What time do most people at your company finish work?
examples.analysis: 多数人 narrows 你们公司 to most of its people. The question word 几点 'what time' sits where the answer would go, before 下班 'get off work'.

collocations.en: the minority defers to the majority; majority rule

related.en: the great majority; very common in speech

meaning: equal (in rights or status); equality

senses.en: equal (in rights, status or treatment)
equality (男女平等 'equality between men and women')

examples.en: Everyone is equal.
examples.analysis: 平等 sits in the 是…的 frame, which states the description as a firm fact. 都 after 大家 covers every member of the group: everyone, without exception.

examples.zh: 你觉得现在男女平等吗？
examples.en: Do you think men and women are equal these days?
examples.analysis: 平等 is the predicate on its own, with no 是: 男女 + 平等. 男女 'men and women' is the usual short pairing here, as in the set phrase 男女平等. 现在 'these days' sets the time, and 你觉得…吗 asks for an opinion.

examples.zh: 我们公司大家都很平等，叫名字就行。
examples.en: Everyone's on an equal footing at our company; just call people by their names.
examples.analysis: Here 平等 is a plain predicate with 很, no 是 and no 的: 大家都很平等 'everyone is equal'. 我们公司 is the topic. The second clause gives the practical result: 叫名字就行 'just use names', where 就行 means 'that's all it takes'.

related.en: fair; just (about rules, deals and outcomes)

meaning: painter; artist (a person who paints)

senses.en: painter; artist who paints or draws

measure.note: 一个画家; 一位画家 is more respectful

examples.en: Her dad is a painter.
examples.analysis: 是 + 画家 gives someone's job. Chinese can leave out 'a' here: 是画家 'is a painter'; 是一个画家 is also correct. 她爸爸 'her dad' needs no 的, as with close family.

examples.en: Which painter do you like?
examples.analysis: 哪 + 个 + 画家 = 'which painter': the measure word 个 sits between 哪 and the noun. The question phrase stays where the answer would go, after 喜欢.

examples.zh: 我不是画家，画画儿只是我的爱好。
examples.en: I'm not a painter. Painting is just a hobby for me.
examples.analysis: 不是 + 画家 denies the job title. The second clause gives the real story: 画画儿 'painting' (verb 画 + noun 画儿 'picture') 只是 'is only' 我的爱好, a hobby, not a job.

hook: 画 'paint' + 家, the ending for a person skilled in a field, as in 作家 'writer' and 科学家 'scientist'.

meaning: to take seriously; to value; to attach importance to

senses.en: to take something seriously; to treat it as important (重视健康)
to value a person or their work; to think highly of

examples.zh: 我们公司很重视这件事。
examples.en: Our company takes this very seriously.
examples.analysis: 重视 + object = 'take seriously, treat as important'. It is a verb of attitude, so 很 can go right before it: 很重视. 这件事 'this matter' counts a matter with 件.

examples.en: You need to take your health seriously.
examples.analysis: 要 + 重视 gives advice: 'you need to take … seriously'. 自己的身体 'your own health' is the object; 身体 often means health, not just the body.

examples.en: He doesn't take his studies very seriously.
examples.analysis: 不太 before 重视 softens the negative to 'not very'. 学习 'studying, schoolwork' is the object, the thing he does not treat as important.

collocations.en: to be valued; to be taken seriously

related.en: to care about; to be concerned for (warmer, about people)
serious; careful (about how you do something)

meaning: English (the language, often English writing)

senses.en: English, the language; often English writing or text (英文名字, 英文菜单)

examples.en: Do you have an English name?
examples.analysis: 英文 describes 名字 directly, with no 的: 英文名字 'English name'. 有 + object + 吗 makes a yes/no question.

examples.en: How do you say this in English?
examples.analysis: 用 + 英文 = 'using English, in English', placed before the verb 说. 怎么说 asks 'how to say'. 这个 at the front is the thing you are pointing at.

examples.en: There's no English on the menu.
examples.analysis: 菜单 + 上 = 'on the menu', a place. 没有 + 英文 says no English text is there; 英文 fits written English like this, on menus and signs.

related.en: English; in mainland usage 学英语 and 说英语 are the more common pairings (英文 leans toward writing and names)

meaning: to take a photo; to have one's photo taken

senses.en: to take a photo; to have one's picture taken (takes no object; 照个相 'take a quick photo')

examples.en: Let's take a picture together!
examples.analysis: 照相 is the verb here and takes no object. 一起 'together' goes before it, and 吧 turns the line into a suggestion. In speech 照相 can also split: 照个相 'take a quick photo'.

examples.en: Excuse me, can I take photos here?
examples.analysis: 可以 + verb + 吗 asks for permission. 照相 needs no object, and 这儿 'here' at the front is the place in question. 请问 opens the question politely.

examples.zh: 手机没电了，不能照相了。
examples.en: My phone's dead, so I can't take photos now.
examples.analysis: 不能 + 照相 = 'can't take photos', and the first clause gives the reason: 没电了 'the battery has run out'. Each 了 marks a change in the situation.

related.en: to take photos; very common today

meaning: to rent out; to let (from the owner's side)

senses.en: to rent out; to let (a room, a flat, a car or bike) to someone

examples.en: Is this apartment for rent?
examples.analysis: 出租 is renting out, from the owner's side; the flat is what is being let. 套 is the measure word for an apartment or house. 吗 makes it a yes/no question.

examples.en: There's a room for rent downstairs.
examples.analysis: 有 + 房间 + 出租: 'there is a room to rent out'. The second verb says what the room is for; Chinese chains the two with no word for 'to' or 'for'.

examples.zh: 我们的房子不出租，要卖。
examples.en: We're not renting our house out; we're selling it.
examples.analysis: 我们的房子 is the topic for both parts. 不 + 出租 turns down one option, and 要卖 gives the plan instead: it is going to be sold.

related.en: to rent (either side: 租房子 'rent a flat')

hook: 出 'out' + 租 'rent': renting out, which is why 出租车 is a car for hire, a taxi.

meaning: to raise one's hand; to put one's hand up

senses.en: to raise one's hand (to ask, answer or vote)

examples.en: If you have a question, please raise your hand.
examples.analysis: 举手 'raise one's hand' already contains its object (手), so no further object follows it. 请 makes the request polite. 有问题 at the front works as an 'if' clause without an 'if' word.

examples.en: Hands up if you want to go!
examples.analysis: 想去的 = 'those who want to go': 的 stands in for 'people'. Then 举手 calls for a quick show of hands, as among friends planning a trip or in a meeting.

examples.en: Nobody raised a hand.
examples.analysis: 没有人 + verb is the usual way to say 'nobody': literally 'there is no one (who) …'. Here it reads as past, 'nobody raised a hand'. 举手 is the action no one took, as when a teacher asks the class a question.

collocations.en: to raise one's hand to ask a question
Hands up! (a sharp command, e.g. from police; for raising a hand in class say 举手)
no trouble at all (a tiny favor)

meaning: notes (written down in class, at a talk or while reading)

senses.en: notes taken in class, at a meeting or while reading

measure.note: 一本笔记 'a book full of notes'; for a set of notes 一份笔记 also works

examples.en: You should take notes in class.
examples.analysis: 笔记 is the object of 记 'to write down': 记笔记 is the standard pairing for 'take notes'. 上课的时候 sets the time, and 要 gives the advice.

examples.zh: 你的笔记能给我看看吗？
examples.en: Could I have a look at your notes?
examples.analysis: 你的笔记 comes first as the topic. 能给我看看吗 'can you let me have a look': 给我 'to me, for me' marks who gets the look, and the doubled 看看 makes it a quick look.

examples.en: I forgot to bring my notes.
examples.analysis: 忘了 + verb phrase = 'forgot to do', with 了 attached to 忘. 笔记 is the object of 带 'to bring'.

related.en: notebook; also short for 笔记本电脑 'laptop'

meaning: common; often seen

senses.en: common; often seen or found (常见病 'a common illness')

examples.en: This illness is very common.
examples.analysis: 常见 'common, often seen' is the predicate, with 很 and no 是. 这个病 'this illness' is the subject; from a doctor, the line is a reassurance.

examples.en: This is a common problem.
examples.analysis: 常见 describes 问题 through 的: 常见的问题 'a common problem'. Without 的, 常见问题 is the set label for 'FAQ' on websites.

examples.zh: 这样的天气在北京不常见。
examples.en: Weather like this isn't common in Beijing.
examples.analysis: 不常见 = 'not common, unusual': 不 negates it as with any adjective. 这样的天气 'weather like this' is the topic, and 在北京 limits where the claim holds.

meaning: not only (… but also …)

senses.en: not only; the first half of 不但…而且/还/也… 'not only … but also …'

examples.zh: 这家饭馆不但便宜，而且好吃。
examples.en: This restaurant isn't just cheap; the food is good too.
examples.analysis: 不但 A，而且 B = 'not only A but also B', with B as the further point. One subject, 这家饭馆, covers both halves, so it comes before 不但.

examples.zh: 他不但没来，也没打电话。
examples.en: Not only did he not show up, he didn't call either.
examples.analysis: 不但 works with a negative too: 不但没来 'not only didn't come'. The second clause adds another failure with 也没 'didn't … either'; 也 does the job 而且 does in other 不但 sentences.

examples.en: It's not just me going; my mom is going too.
examples.analysis: With two different subjects, 不但 normally goes before the first one: 不但我去. The second clause names its own subject and adds 也 'also'.

related.en: and also; moreover (the usual second half)
although (another two-part pattern: 虽然…但是…)

meaning: to treat (someone to a meal or drinks); to pay for everyone

senses.en: to treat; to pay for a meal or outing for others (我请客 'it's on me')
to invite guests; to host a dinner

examples.en: Who's treating today?
examples.analysis: 谁 'who' sits in the subject slot, where the answer will go. 请客 'treat others, pay for them' needs no object, and 今天 sets the occasion.

examples.zh: 你帮了我这么多，今天我请客吧。
examples.en: You've helped me so much. Let me treat you today.
examples.analysis: 请客 is the offer to pay, here as thanks for a favor: 我请客 'it's on me'. 吧 makes it a friendly proposal. The first clause gives the reason with no word for 'because', and 这么多 'so much' says how big the help was.

examples.zh: 你上次说请客，还没请呢！
examples.en: You said you'd treat us last time, and you still haven't!
examples.analysis: 说请客 = 'said you'd treat us'. After 请客 has been said once, 请 alone is enough: 还没请呢 'still haven't (treated)', where 还没…呢 marks something still pending.

collocations.en: to treat people to a meal

related.en: to invite; to treat (请你吃饭 'take you out for a meal')
to pay the bill (at a restaurant)
